title: Scalars and vectors; Describing motion
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: K01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; K01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; K01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: K01-1#N.2, MS05-1#N.4, K01-1#N.5, MS05-1#N.10, K01-1#N.10, MS05-1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Acceleration
items.clue: Rate of change of velocity, in m s⁻².

items.label: Displacement
items.clue: The change in position: a vector quantity.

items.label: Average speed
items.clue: Whole path length divided by whole time taken: a scalar.

items.label: Distance
items.clue: Total length of the path: a scalar that is never negative.

questions.stem: A runner moves along a straight track. Her position x is measured from a marker on the track. She starts at x = +30 m, runs to x = +70 m, then turns around and runs to x = −20 m, where she stops. What is her displacement?

A hiker walks 5 m east and then 9 m west along a straight path. Student 1 takes east as the positive direction; Student 2 takes west as the positive direction. Each finds the hiker's resultant displacement as a signed component. Which statement correctly compares their results?

options.text: Only Student 1 can be right, as east has to be the positive direction.
Student 1 gets −4 m and Student 2 gets +4 m, and both results mean 4 m west.
Both get +4 m, by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger.
Both get 14 m, since the two walks simply add to give the resultant.

questions.stem: An object moves along a straight line, with positive taken to the right. At one instant its velocity is −3.0 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is +2.0 m s⁻². The acceleration stays constant. Which describes the motion of the object?

options.text: Moving left and slowing down; it will then stop and stay at rest.
Moving left and speeding up, since its acceleration is positive.
Moving left and slowing down; later it will move off to the right.
Moving right and speeding up, in the direction of its acceleration.

questions.stem: A small block moves up a straight ramp inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Student 1 resolves the block's velocity into horizontal and vertical components. Student 2 resolves the same velocity using an x-axis along the ramp and a y-axis perpendicular to the ramp. Which statement about their results is correct?

options.text: Their components must match, since both pairs describe one velocity.
Their components differ, but each pair combines to give the same velocity.
Student 2's are not proper components, as components are horizontal and vertical.
Their components differ, so the two students find different speeds.

questions.stem: A car travels 3.0 km along a straight road at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹, then returns along the same road to its starting point at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. What are its average speed and its average velocity for the whole journey?

options.text: Average speed 12.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 12 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity −2.5 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: A robot vacuum moves 1.1 m east and then 1.6 m north, each along a straight line. What is the magnitude of its displacement from its starting point?
